title: Data Center Is Fined $1.1 Million for Operating 62 Power Generators

reading.body:
This is a permitting and compliance failure at the power layer of a data center build, not a failure of a model or a decision system. State inspectors found 62 natural-gas generators, tractor-trailer sized and rated at 2,000 kilowatts, at a Vineland construction site in late July, and none held the permits required for installation or operation. DataOne was fined $1.07 million under the Air Pollution Control Act, which state officials described as the largest such fine issued to a New Jersey data center operator.

The generators were in place at a campus that is not finished and is already partly in use. That is where the failure sits: generation capacity was installed and run ahead of the authorization the state requires. Catching it needed a permit review before installation or an inspection before operation, and it was a state inspection in late July that surfaced it. The planned campus is 2.6 million square feet and needs 350 megawatts.

What is not established is any intent to operate without permits. The federal lawsuit filed by homeowners over noise is a claim, not a finding, and the Cumberland County Health Department violation orders are separate from the air pollution fine. The reporting also does not establish that any AI system was involved in the siting, the power design or the running of the generators.

reports.title: Data Center Is Fined $1.1 Million for Operating 62 Power Generators

summary:
New Jersey fined DataOne $1.07 million after state inspectors found 62 tractor-trailer-size natural-gas generators at its Vineland data center construction site in late July. The 2,000-kilowatt generators lacked required permits to be installed or operated. The fine, for violating the Air Pollution Control Act, is the largest ever issued to a New Jersey data center operator, state officials said.

The planned Vineland campus is 2.6 million square feet and needs 350 megawatts, enough to power a medium-size city, with completion set for the end of the year. Some of it is already in use. The site has drawn complaints since the zoning process. Homeowners have filed a federal lawsuit over persistent noise, and the Cumberland County Health Department issued violation orders to DataOne for excessive noise.
